title: What the $200 Minimum Fee Covers for Small Stump Jobs
meta_description: A single small stump still comes with a $200 minimum fee. Here's what that minimum actually covers and why it applies regardless of job size.
lede: A single small stump can feel like it shouldn't cost much, which makes the $200 minimum fee worth actually explaining.
excerpt: Why a $200 minimum fee applies even to the smallest stump grinding job.

sections.heading: Mobilization Costs the Same Regardless of Size
paragraphs: Getting equipment and a crew to a property costs roughly the same whether the job is one small stump or several large ones. The $200 minimum fee reflects that baseline cost of showing up and getting set up.

sections.heading: It Applies to All Stump Grinding Work
paragraphs: This isn't a fee that only kicks in under certain conditions. It applies to all stump grinding work, which makes pricing predictable rather than dependent on negotiating a smaller job down.

sections.heading: How This Plays Into Multi-Stump Jobs
paragraphs: If there's more than one stump on a property, grouping them into a single visit means that mobilization cost is effectively spread across all of them rather than paid separately for each.

sections.heading: Getting an Exact Number
paragraphs: For an exact quote on a specific stump, the online cost calculator or a same-day, no-obligation quote both give real numbers rather than a general estimate.

faqs.q: Why is there a minimum fee for a single small stump?
faqs.a: It reflects the baseline cost of mobilizing equipment and a crew, which is roughly the same regardless of job size.

faqs.q: Does the minimum fee apply to every job?
faqs.a: Yes, it applies to all stump grinding work, not just certain conditions.

faqs.q: Is it cheaper per stump if I have more than one?
faqs.a: Generally yes, since grouping multiple stumps into one visit spreads the mobilization cost across all of them.
